transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Valley Head of AI), Liam O'Connor (Valley Security Architect), Janelle Park (Valley Dir. Product)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a security-focused POC: agree success criteria, identify workloads for benchmarks, align on compliance docs (SOC 2/ISO), SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit log needs, and confirm timeline for pilot infrastructure (VPC/on-prem options).

Topics:
- Success criteria and KPIs (latency, cost, accuracy/regression tolerance)
- Workload sizing and benchmark profiles
- Security/compliance checklist: SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, data residency
- Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem)
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick intro from our side, I'm Maya, AE, and Diego's our solutions engineer, we'll drive the scoping.
[00:12] Priya Singh: Hi all, Priya here. We're excited to move the pilot forward, security is top of mind so Liam's on to cover those constraints.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: Hey, yes hi. Our primary ask is: we need to validate that any hosted pilot can meet our SOC 2 expectations, SSO/SAML integration, and that audit trails are available for the user actions. Also KMS for key management.
[00:33] Diego Alvarez: Great, understood. We'll outline what Redwood can share: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO certificates summary, SAML SSO flows, RBAC capabilities, and detailed audit log schema.
[00:44] Janelle Park: Timeline wise we want a two-week pilot for evaluation and a decision within 6 weeks. Is that feasible?
[00:50] Maya Chen: Two-week active benchmark window is doable, upstream prep will take a week to set up access and share samples. So total ~4-6 weeks for decision sounds reasonable.
[00:59] Priya Singh: Success criteria — we have three pillars: security/compliance acceptance, performance (latency P95 < 400ms for our documents), and cost — unit cost must be within our forecasted budget, Diego can you help translate unit cost?
[01:14] Diego Alvarez: Yep, we'll map token-level pricing to your expected throughput. We recommend three benchmark workloads: 1) triage summarization (short docs, seq len ~512), 2) large note generation (seq len ~2k), 3) batch embeddings for search (bulk embedding throughput). We'll measure latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k ops.
[01:33] Liam O'Connor: On the security checklist, a few specifics: 1) SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, 2) ISO 27001 evidence ideal, 3) SSO with SAML 2.0 and provisioning (SCIM), 4) RBAC with audit trails, 5) ability to use our KMS/HSM for keys or dedicated key wrap, 6) VPC peering or private link for network isolation, 7) data residency controls and retention policies.
[01:58] Maya Chen: That's the usual ask, we have SOC 2 Type II report we can share under NDA, we also have an ISO summary. For keys we support bring-your-own-key via KMS integrations for the Private deployment and Dedicated can be configured with customer-managed keys depending on contract. Hosted has AES encryption at rest with Redwood-managed keys but we can discuss enclave options for sensitive data.
[02:21] Priya Singh: Could you clarify the differences between hosted and dedicated/private re: audit logs and RBAC?
[02:28] Diego Alvarez: Sure — hosted gives standard RBAC in the console, audit logs for admin actions kept for X days (we'll confirm retention). Dedicated provides tenant-level isolation, extended log retention and can forward logs to your SIEM via secure export. Private (VPC/on-prem) puts control in your network, you get full log ownership and can route to your own logging stack.
[02:49] Janelle Park: For our compliance team, they need sample audit log entries and schema to validate mappings to our SIEM.
[02:56] Maya Chen: We'll include sample log snippets — login events, model invocation, policy changes, key usage — Diego will attach a CSV / JSON schema in the follow-up.
[03:06] Liam O'Connor: Also want to confirm SAML metadata exchange and SCIM provisioning. We want automated provisioning and deprovisioning for the pilot users.
[03:14] Diego Alvarez: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning for enterprise accounts. For hosted pilot we can do SAML integration in the test org; for Private it'll be within your IdP and network. We'll draft steps to exchange metadata and do a test.
[03:29] Priya Singh: Data residency — our legal requires that PHI-related processing stays in region us-east-1 and logs not forwarded outside. Can Redwood pin region for pilot?
[03:37] Maya Chen: For Dedicated and Private yes; hosted we can route to specific regions depending on availability. For the pilot we can provision a region-bound instance to satisfy residency. We'll note that Dedicated gives stronger guarantees.
[03:50] Janelle Park: Benchmarks — Diego, walk us through typical test matrix and what you need from our side.
[03:55] Diego Alvarez: We'll define three workloads as I said. For each: target QPS, sequence lengths, prompt templates, expected concurrency. Ideally you provide redacted sample payloads and a baseline RPS. We'll run controlled runs measuring P50/P95/P99 latencies, cost per 1k tokens, and qualitative checks for output quality/regressions vs your golden prompts.
[04:18] Priya Singh: Quality regressions — we need a pass/fail tolerance e.g., BLEU/ROUGE or manual evals?
[04:24] Diego Alvarez: We recommend a mix: automated metrics for basic checks and a small human eval set for semantic correctness. We can help set up eval harness and compare model variants.
[04:34] Liam O'Connor: From infra side, for Dedicated we need network diagram, firewall rules, and certificate pinning options. We'll also need to validate KMS integration — do you support AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault?
[04:45] Maya Chen: Yes, we support AWS KMS for Private and Dedicated; Azure Key Vault is on roadmap but we've done customer integrations via key wrap. We'll put exact compatibility and steps in the follow-up.
[04:55] Janelle Park: Any changes to model weights or retraining during pilot? We want to avoid data leakage.
[05:01] Diego Alvarez: We do not retrain customer models on your data during the pilot. For hosted, default is no persistent training. We can also enable strict data isolation for Dedicated and Private.
[05:10] Priya Singh: OK. For the pilot acceptance criteria, can we list them clearly?
[05:16] Maya Chen: Sure — draft acceptance criteria on the call: 1) Security: SOC 2 Type II review complete, SAML SSO working, audit logs validated and forwarded to Valley SIEM, KMS either integrated or acceptable alternative. 2) Performance: P95 under 400ms for triage workload, P95 under 1.2s for large note generation, embedding throughput X. 3) Quality: No major regressions vs golden prompts (<=5% failure rate on human eval). 4) Cost: Unit cost within 15% of Valley forecast.
[05:46] Priya Singh: That looks good, we'll formalize thresholds.
[05:50] Liam O'Connor: On logging retention, our security policy requires 1 year retention and ability to export logs on demand. Is that possible?
[05:58] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated/Private can meet that with long retention and log export. Hosted may have shorter retention; we can offer extended retention as an add-on for enterprise pilots.
[06:08] Maya Chen: Quick note on benchmarks: we'll include quantized model variants if you want cost-optimized runs — Diego will outline expected cost/latency tradeoffs for FP16 vs 8-bit quant.
[06:18] Diego Alvarez: For benchmarking we'll run base model for accuracy and a quantized variant for cost profile. We'll capture per-token latency, GPU utilization, and estimated dollars per 1k tokens.
[06:29] Janelle Park: For decision timeline, we'll need a two-week active test and internal security review; decision meeting scheduled 6 weeks from now.
[06:36] Maya Chen: We'll target delivery of security docs by Monday (2026-09-21) and benchmark plan by Thursday (2026-09-24) — then run tests the week after.
[06:46] Priya Singh: On legal, we'll also need a data processing addendum and standard SOC 2 privacy appendix.
[06:54] Maya Chen: Legal will prepare a draft NDA/DPA and point to our standard DPA template; we'll share links.
[07:02] Liam O'Connor: One more: need to know whether Redwood preserves prompt logs or raw input.
[07:07] Diego Alvarez: We have configurable logging. For hosted, by default we log metadata and may store prompts for short-term debugging; we can opt-out or redact inputs. Dedicated/Private gives you full control. We'll document defaults and options.
[07:20] Priya Singh: Great. Any blockers to start?
[07:22] Maya Chen: No blockers on our side — action items and docs capture the remaining work.
[07:27] Janelle Park: OK let's recap.
[07:29] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya sends SOC 2 and ISO summary; Diego sends benchmark plan and sample log schema; Valley sends redacted workloads and network/KMS constraints; schedule technical deep dive with Liam for VPC/Dedicated details. Decision target 6 weeks.
[07:45] Priya Singh: Thanks everyone, we'll be in touch and we'll expect the docs and plan.
[07:49] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep dive.

End of transcript.
